claim.supported_scope: A planned two-group fixed-size label-permutation procedure using 5,000 through 10,000 usable full plsc_v2 re-estimations per group, attenuation-corrected parameter differences, and a paired PLSc-aware measurement-invariance hierarchy.
claim.estimand: The conditional randomization distribution of Group A minus Group B attenuation-corrected PLSc paths and loadings, plus configural, compositional, mean, and variance invariance diagnostics, under exchangeable labels and the frozen two-group design.
assumptions: Exactly two selected groups share the same reflective model, indicators, preprocessing, missing-data policy, estimator settings, and canonical orientation.
Group labels are exchangeable under the tested null and group sizes remain fixed in every permutation.
Every usable permutation independently re-estimates complete PLSc v2 solutions for both groups.
exclusions: More than two groups, case weights, interactions, higher-order constructs, PCA weighting, matrix-only input, parametric MGA, and bootstrap MGA are excluded.
Standard-PLS MICOM or permutation-MGA output cannot be relabeled or reused as PLSc consistent-permutation evidence.
A significant difference is not evidence of causality, practical importance, semantic group equivalence, or measurement invariance.
warnings: Structural comparisons require at least partial invariance for the involved constructs under the paired PLSc-aware invariance result.
Failed or inadmissible PLSc permutation fits must be disclosed and may not silently change the requested usable distribution.

equations.expression: (D*_A,b, D*_B,b) = permute_labels_without_replacement(D_A union D_B, n_A, n_B, seed_b)

references.citation: Dijkstra and Henseler (2015), Consistent Partial Least Squares Path Modeling
Chin and Dibbern (2010), An Introduction to a Permutation Based Procedure for Multi-Group PLS Analysis
Henseler, Ringle, and Sarstedt (2016), Testing Measurement Invariance of Composites Using Partial Least Squares
Planned independent Python PLSc label-permutation and measurement-invariance implementation

simulations.design: Equal-parameter reflective two-group models spanning sample size, imbalance, reliability, collinearity, nonnormality, and group-label prevalence.
simulations.seed_policy: Scenario and permutation indexed streams independent of worker count; QuickPLS and the independent reference receive identical assignments.
simulations.acceptance_rule: At each preregistered supported cell, empirical rejection rates must lie within their binomial calibration bands and the pooled false-rejection upper envelope must not exceed the independently reviewed threshold.

simulations.design: Known path, loading, composition, mean, and variance differences across balanced and imbalanced reflective two-group designs.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen scenario-indexed data streams and domain-separated permutation streams.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Preregistered identifiable effects must meet the frozen power and direction-recovery thresholds while null parameters remain calibrated.

simulations.design: Weak-reliability and small-group cells that yield improper rho_A, inadmissible corrected correlations, nonconvergence, singularity, or an exhausted attempt cap.
simulations.seed_policy: Every attempted assignment has a stable index and is never replaced by a new stream identity.
simulations.acceptance_rule: QuickPLS and the independent reference must agree on every assignment and failure category, and no inference may be emitted after the usable target fails within the frozen cap.

boundaries.case: An original or permuted group produces improper rho_A, an inadmissible corrected correlation, nonconvergence, singularity, or nonfinite estimates.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Original-fit failure blocks the run; a permutation-fit failure is explicitly counted and the run fails if the usable target cannot be reached within the fixed cap.

boundaries.case: The request has other than two groups, too few complete cases, mismatched configural models, weights, interactions, higher-order constructs, PCA weighting, matrix-only input, or an out-of-range permutation count.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Typed setup validation blocks execution with the exact condition identified.

boundaries.case: Group A and B are swapped or rows and constructs are consistently reordered.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Mapped differences reverse sign on group swap, two-sided probabilities remain equal, and reordered results agree within tolerance.

boundaries.case: The same recipe and seed execute under all supported worker counts and schedules.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Assignments, failures, usable ordering, distributions, probabilities, and invariance payloads are exactly equal.

boundaries.case: Group identity, assignment plan, counts, parameter difference, probability, invariance row, dataset fingerprint, or method identity is changed.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict project validation rejects the archive rather than displaying or exporting the changed result.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject a result whose consistent-permutation identity differs from the typed PLSc group recipe.
Reject a plsc_permutation_v1 artifact paired with ordinary PLS or incompatible PLSc/invariance versions.
Reject a result whose pooled/group complete-case manifests or dataset fingerprint no longer match.
Reject any changed archive member whose checksum differs.
Reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, nonfinite values, bad counts, assignments, differences, probabilities, invariance hierarchy, or reasons.
Never reinterpret pls_mga_permutation_v1/v2 or micom_v1/v2 output as PLSc consistent-permutation evidence.

persistence.legacy_policy: Only a typed plsc_permutation_v1 artifact with matching PLSc-aware invariance identity may satisfy this contract.

setup_controls: Group column and exact Group A/B values
applicability_blockers: Unsupported PLSc shape or resampling count
native.gui_cli_parity_rule: For the same recipe, seed, method versions, group selection, and dataset fingerprint, GUI and CLI assignments and analytical payloads must be exactly equal apart from operational timestamps.
accessibility_rules: Invariance state and parameter tables are keyboard and screen-reader accessible.
Significance, invariance failures, warnings, and unavailable states never rely only on color or pointer interaction.
